title: Hidden and Revealed: The Sun, the Moon, and the Ambassador's Mysteries
summary: A sustained treatment of the visible mysteries: hidden and revealed members in the body as likeness of the Father; the First Man clothed in the elements, his swallowed light becoming the river of judgment from within the archons; the three Rocks of Glory (Pillar, Land of Light upon Land of Darkness, Jesus the Radiance) set in the outer worlds; love defined as the bond of the Greatness and hatred as the first death; the three things and seven reasons for Adam's forming as sealed icon and microcosm; and finally the central image of sun and night as the two daily mysteries by which heaven and hell are made legible to creation.
organizing_principle: Building toward the central image of the sun and night as the two visible mysteries. The section moves from body-correspondence through the foundational definitions of love and hate to Adam as icon-bearer, culminating in the sun-and-Ambassador triple chapter.
